Subject: Unit economics deep dive — post-call recap and next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today, Alex & Meghan — really appreciate the clear context on how FintechX plans to use embeddings + chat for transaction classification and customer support triage. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- TL;DR: You’re evaluating a pilot that will: (1) run classification embeddings for 6M monthly transactions (~30M tokens/month from embeddings + 20M tokens/month for chat/assist prompts => ~50M tokens/month total), (2) surface one primary LLM-powered feature in your mobile app (support triage), and (3) keep throughput spikes up to 2–3x on business days.

Key numbers we discussed (please correct if I’ve misread):
- Estimated monthly token volume (start): ~50M tokens/month
- Target budget range (pilot): $6k–$12k/month
- Desired target economics: unit cost target of ~$10–$15 per 1M tokens (net after any committed discounts) to hit feature-level margin targets

Ask / next steps:
1) I’m attaching an updated unit econ workbook (FintechX_unit_econ_v2.xlsx) with scenarios at 25M/50M/150M tokens and our suggested pricing bands. Please drop in any real cost assumptions (hosting, SRE, storage) on tab “Customer inputs.”
2) Can you confirm expected pilot length and # of DAUs for the triage feature? That will let us produce $/feature and CAC-payback sensitivity.
3) I’m looping in David (Solutions) and Neha (Sales Ops) to help validate throughput and draft a committed-capacity proposal that matches your budget.

If agreeable, we’ll follow up with a short committed-capacity quote and a canary rollout plan (2-week pilot + autoscale buffer) by Friday.

Subject: Re: Unit economics deep dive — post-call recap and next steps

Alex — thanks, good to see the scale plan. Below is a concise worked example (we’ll dump full sensitivity scenarios into the attached workbook and the proposal). I’ll also flag items that will affect CAC payback and margin.

Assumptions (worked example):
- Pilot volumes: 50M tokens/month; Scale: 200M tokens/month.
- Redwood list pricing assumption (before commit discount): $20 / 1M tokens for generation/chat + $6 / 1M tokens for embeddings (we combine for blended token rate in examples).
- Example commit discounts: 40% at 50M (pilot commit) => blended $/1M = $15; 55% at 200M => blended $/1M = $11.7 (we’ll propose $12 for simplicity).
- Inference infra & SRE (customer-facing marginal costs to FintechX): we recommend modeling $2.0 / 1M tokens for infra/SRE/ops on top of Redwood unit cost as a conservative estimate (this can be reduced with caching/batching optimizations).

Worked examples: 
1) 50M tokens/month at $15 / 1M tokens => Redwood cost = $750 / month. + infra/SRE $100 = $850 total monthly inference cost.
   - If triage feature reaches 10k MAUs (monthly active users) and drives 50k feature-usage events/month (avg 5 events/user), then cost per feature-use = $850 / 50k = $0.017; cost per MAU = $850 / 10k = $0.085.
   - If price per MAU contribution target is $1.50, gross margin contribution per MAU = $1.50 - $0.085 = $1.415 (very healthy). CAC payback depends on CAC — example: if CAC = $30, then payback = 30 / 1.415 ≈ 21 months; if you target 6–9 month payback, CAC should be ≤ $9–$13.

2) 200M tokens/month at $12 / 1M tokens => Redwood cost = $2,400 / month. + infra/SRE $400 = $2,800 total monthly inference cost.
   - If at scale triage reaches 40k MAUs and 200k feature events/month, cost per feature-use = $2,800 / 200k = $0.014; cost per MAU = $2,800 / 40k = $0.07.
   - With $1.50 contribution per MAU, margin per MAU = $1.43. CAC payback: if CAC = $30, payback ≈ 21 months; if CAC = $10, payback ≈ 7 months.

Notes and levers: 
- Caching & batching: with prefix/KV caching and optimized batching we’ve seen effective infra/SRE marginal costs drop from $2.0 to $0.5 / 1M tokens for similar workloads — this materially improves unit economics and payback.
- Feature design: reducing average events per MAU (or moving some logic to cheaper deterministic rules) lowers token volumes per MAU.
- Pricing levers: a small increase in per-MAU monetization (e.g., $0.25 incremental) can cut CAC payback by several months.

Next from Redwood: David will validate throughput and provide a recommended autoscale buffer; Neha will draft a pilot committed-capacity quote for ~$10k/month with a 30-day PO flow. We’ll send the proposal + DocuSign link by EOD Friday.

Shall we schedule a quick 20-min sync with your PM to confirm DAU/feature-usage assumptions?

Best,
Marissa

Alex — quick note from the infra side on throughput and cost assumptions: 
- We can sustain 3x spikes with autoscale buffer using a 2-node warm pool for the pilot. That adds ~+$250/month infra margin to the numbers Marissa shared (included in the conservative $2.0 / 1M token estimate).

- Data residency: we can provision pilot on US-region private tenancy. SLA addendum and SOC2 artifacts attached in Redwood_pricing_terms_v1.pdf.
